roots.name: Linux
roots.description: Core Linux command-line tools for file management, text processing, process control, and system administration. The commands in this category run on Linux and most Unix systems; macOS support is noted per command where it differs.

roots.name: Git
roots.description: Git version control commands for tracking changes, collaborating on code, managing branches, and maintaining project history. Every command in this category is invoked as a subcommand of the `git` binary and carries a fully-qualified slug (e.g. git-commit, git-clone) to guarantee global uniqueness.

roots.name: Bash
roots.description: Bash shell built-in commands and scripting constructs. These are not external programs but features of the Bash shell itself, available in any Bash session without additional installation.

roots.name: Docker
roots.description: Docker container management commands for building, running, inspecting, and orchestrating containerized applications. All commands are subcommands of the docker CLI binary.

roots.name: Networking
roots.description: Network diagnostic, configuration, and transfer commands for inspecting connectivity, managing interfaces, transferring data, and troubleshooting network issues from the command line.

roots.name: SSH
roots.description: Secure Shell commands for remote access, file transfer, tunneling, and key management. SSH is the foundation of secure remote system administration.

roots.name: Permissions
roots.description: File permission and ownership commands for controlling access to files and directories on Unix-like systems. Understanding permissions is fundamental to system security.

roots.name: Processes
roots.description: Process management commands for inspecting, controlling, and terminating running processes. Essential for system monitoring, debugging, and resource management.

roots.name: Unix
roots.description: Core Unix commands and concepts shared across BSD, macOS, and other POSIX-compliant systems. Commands here work on any Unix-like OS, not just Linux.

roots.name: PowerShell
roots.description: PowerShell cmdlets and scripting constructs for Windows and cross-platform system administration. PowerShell operates on objects rather than text streams, offering a fundamentally different approach from traditional Unix shells.

roots.name: Kubernetes
roots.description: Kubernetes cluster management commands using kubectl and related tools. Covers pod lifecycle, deployments, services, configuration, and cluster operations.

roots.name: Kernel
roots.description: Linux kernel interaction commands for tuning kernel parameters, loading modules, and inspecting kernel state. These commands modify or query the running kernel directly.

roots.name: System Calls
roots.description: Linux system call interfaces accessible from the command line and shell scripts. Understanding system calls bridges the gap between shell usage and operating system internals.

roots.name: Shell Scripting
roots.description: Shell scripting constructs, patterns, and utilities for writing robust automation scripts. Covers control flow, variable handling, argument parsing, and scripting best practices.

roots.name: Cron
roots.description: Scheduled task management with cron, at, and related utilities. Covers crontab syntax, scheduling patterns, and best practices for reliable job scheduling.

roots.name: Regex
roots.description: Regular expression syntax, patterns, and command-line tools for pattern matching. Covers POSIX BRE/ERE, PCRE, and practical regex usage in grep, sed, awk, and other tools.

roots.name: Text Processing
roots.description: Text manipulation and transformation commands for filtering, reformatting, sorting, and analyzing text data. The foundation of Unix pipeline-based data processing.

roots.name: File Systems
roots.description: File system management commands for mounting, unmounting, checking, and inspecting disk usage and filesystem state. Covers both traditional and modern Linux file systems.

roots.name: Package Managers
roots.description: System and language package management commands for installing, updating, removing, and querying software packages across distributions and ecosystems.

roots.name: Cloud CLI
roots.description: Cloud provider CLI tools for managing infrastructure, services, and deployments from the command line. Covers AWS CLI, gcloud, and Azure CLI patterns.

roots.name: DevOps Utilities
roots.description: Cross-cutting DevOps tools for CI/CD, infrastructure management, monitoring, and deployment automation. These utilities bridge development and operations workflows.
